commitments.target: 500 crore to 600 crore capex broadly for FY27
commitments.quote: So broadly, it will be about INR 500 crore to INR 600 crore.
commitments.speaker: Mayank Singhal

commitments.target: commercialize 8 to 10 new molecules with 5 already commercialized
commitments.quote: We are on track to commercialize 8 to 10 new molecules with 5 molecules already commercialized.
commitments.speaker: Mayank Singhal

commitments.target: long-term gross profit margin between 50% to 52%
commitments.quote: As we guided in the past, we continue to maintain our long-term GP margin guidance between 50% to 52%, and we continue to move with that.
commitments.speaker: Mayank Singhal

claims.claim: Reported revenue of INR 13,757 million for Q3 FY26
claims.quote: For quarter 3 FY26, we reported revenue of INR 13,757 million, which comes on the back of a high base of the previous years.

claims.claim: Pharma platform delivered a 50% year-on-year growth
claims.quote: Now coming to Pharma, we have delivered a 50% year-on-year growth.

claims.claim: Gross margin expanded to 59% during the quarter supported by product mix and cost discipline
claims.quote: On other financial metrices, our gross margin expanded to 59% during the quarter, supported by a favorable product mix and cost discipline.

claims.claim: Trade working capital in terms of days of sales increased to 139 days
claims.quote: Our trade working capital in terms of days of sales has increased to 139 days and reflects current market conditions, we expect to improve this as market scenario normalizes in the coming quarters.

claims.claim: Domestic agrochemical demand remained subdued due to high channel inventory and low commodity prices
claims.quote: Domestic agrochemical demand remains subdued due to high channel inventory, low commodity prices, delay in normalization of biological portfolio post regulatory headwind and specific impact from lower demand in a few target crops for PI.

claims.claim: Net profit includes write-back of contingent consideration of INR 1,260 million offset by retirement benefits provisioning
claims.quote: During the quarter, net profit includes an exceptional income in our pharma business on account for a write-back of contingent consideration of INR 1,260 million which has been partly offset by additional provisioning of retirement benefits as per New Labour Code to the tune of INR 209 million.

analyst_concerns.question: Analyst pressed for details on whether expected Q4 and FY27 growth is volume or value, and the magnitude.
analyst_concerns.quote: So, first question is on the guidance. When you say growth resuming in fourth quarter, is it only a sequential growth that you are talking about or you even expect a Y-o-Y growth and what this growth is really? Is it like a volume growth that you are alluding to? Or do you even expect a revenue growth or a value growth in the fourth quarter?

analyst_concerns.question: Analyst asked about the gap between high delivered gross margins and the long-term guidance of 50-52%.
analyst_concerns.quote: So, we have been delivering quite good kind of gross margins for last few quarters. What is the gap between what is your expectations on a sustainable basis? And what we are delivering? What is this gap attributed to?

analyst_concerns.question: Analyst inquired about heavy quarterly EBITDA losses in pharma and biologics and peak investment timeline.
analyst_concerns.quote: Now if you look at the numbers, we are heavily investing in these businesses, and we are roughly at a INR 75 crore, INR 80 crore quarterly EBITDA loss in these segments So, how should we think about the investments from our medium to longer term? And are we at the peak of the investment in these businesses? And going ahead, the investment should move in line with our overall OPEX?

analyst_concerns.question: Analyst pressed on the sharp increase in working capital days from 68 to 139 days.
analyst_concerns.quote: So, my second question, Sanjay, if you can throw some light, there has been an increase in the working capital quite sharply, almost from 68 days to 139 days Y-o-Y. So, could you please explain and how we should expect the intensity of working capital coming down?
